subject: Escalation: Parkmont Health interactive streams dropping -> client retry storm & 5xx/429 spike (needs exec attention)
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@parkmont.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parkmont Health SRE <sre@parkmont.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions — repeated drops and client-side timeouts (observed 14:00-14:30 PDT)

Hi Evelyn,

We're seeing a sharp rise in dropped streaming sessions and a following retry spiral from our web clients between 14:00-14:30 PDT. Symptoms: the client-side SDK reports idle disconnects (no DATA frames) after ~18s and then does aggressive backoff/retry that floods our edge with new connections — that correlates with 429s and some 5xx spikes on your side. Attached is a HAR export and a short SLI screenshot.

Impact: around ~12% of active sessions experienced one or more forced reconnects during a 30-minute window; we've had to disable a non-critical background streaming job to keep the app usable. This is impacting our pilot cohort, and the execs are asking for an immediate timeline.

Can you confirm whether there was any change to streaming keepalive intervals, a routing policy change, or a capacity shift in us-west-2 at 13:50 PDT?

--
Aaron
SRE, Parkmont Health

Attachments: parkmont_error_snapshot.har (HAR), parkmont_sli_9-14.png (PNG)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@parkmont.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions — quick triage notes

Evelyn / Monica — initial findings from the first pass:
- No scheduled deployment or config change in us-west-2 at 13:50 PDT in our change logs.
- We saw a transient spike in CPU steal on a subset of shared workers servicing Parkmont routes from 13:55-14:08 PDT (~2.6x baseline). Those workers then reported a rise in idle connection timeouts (server-perceived inactivity) and closed sessions.
- KV cache hit-rate for Parkmont routes dropped from 78% -> 42% during the window; suspect an LRU churn coincident with increased other-tenant load.
- Downstream result: lots of short reconnects (client retries) hitting the front‑end LB and producing 429 throttles under the configured per-tenant ephemeral limit.

Temporary mitigations I've applied (rolling):
1) Increased per-route connection window and raised soft concurrency limits for Parkmont on a temporary policy.
2) Bumped the keepalive ping interval tolerance on the streaming proxy to accept 25s quiet periods (was 18s).

I'll continue to gather worker-level traces and a timeline. If we confirm noisy neighbor or capacity pressure we'll move Parkmont to a warm reserved pool.

Connor
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@parkmont.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parkmont Health SRE <sre@parkmont.health>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions — more logs attached

Thanks Connor — that aligns with what we see. I attached an anonymized SDK log snippet in the HAR (client internal IDs removed). The client retries are aggressive: initial backoff is ~200ms and doubles, but because the session dies quickly the clients re-establish many concurrent streams in the same second which bursts your front end.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can Redwood deploy a short-term rate-limiter at the edge to smooth replay storms from clients?
- If possible, signal the SDK to apply a softer retry strategy (we can accept a minor increase in single-request latency but not mass reconnects).

Parkmont execs are on standby; if we can't contain the storm this afternoon they'll ask for account credits and a postmortem.

Aaron
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation briefing (exec ask) — Parkmont Health P1 follow-up

Team — Parkmont's execs requested an update and potential credit approval this morning. Key points to present:
- Impact summary: ~12% session impact during 14:00-14:30 PDT, leading to an observed 3x increase in 429s for their tenant and client retry amplification.
- Root-cause hypotheses: noisy neighbor capacity spike -> KV cache churn -> server-perceived idle -> client retries -> front-end throttle cascade.
- Immediate mitigations implemented: temporary per-route concurrency bump + extended keepalive tolerance (Connor).
- Open asks for execs: 1) Temporary account credit for the pilot (ballpark $3k) 2) Commitment to move Parkmont to a warm reserved pool for peak hours next week 3) Postmortem within 72 hours with action items.

Vivek: can you confirm whether we have capacity in our reserved pool for a same‑day warm move (us-west-2)? Aditya: please prepare a one-slide summary & estimated credit table for the customer-facing exec. Monica/Connor: continue deep triage and root confirmation. I'll join Parkmont's bridge at 8:30 PDT.

Evelyn
